final.label: value-rows-need-consumer-or-provenance
final.disposition: widen_existing (check 1). Check 1 keeps its conversion-row trigger (kind a) and gains two triggers from the corpus: (b) a round placeholder literal assigned to a model-parameter field in a test fixture with no comment (PR 2176, comment 2948257220, a suggestion block; fixed at 8a6db7243 (:94, :571, :1029, :1174), visible at the head 429249ead6 (:95, :575, :1033, :1178)), and (c) an opaque expected literal (a hex digest, a frozen table) whose origin no comment, document or register names (asim PR 244, comment 4020335622, a question; fixed at 927d501a86, approved at 63c5b8a12c). All three ask one question in Wade's terms: what depends on this exact value, or where did it come from. The remedy stays on the test side: drop the row, add the don't-care comment, or add the provenance comment and the register row. All three refuters said fix; every fix is folded. Where the precision and executability lenses disagreed on the kind (b) discriminator, the executability form (the production producer evaluated on the fixture's own values) is used, because it is a computation an agent can run; the precision form (a real model's value) needs model knowledge the diff does not give.

skill_entry.name: 1. Value-pinning rows need a consumer; fixture placeholders need a don't-care comment; opaque expected literals need a provenance
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of three. (a) Conversion row: a test hunk adds a runtime assertion whose expected literal or table entry differs from the bits the same test wrote or read back earlier by a conversion, rounding (ties included), flush, saturation or class change (NaN to inf, denormal to zero). A pure widening is no difference; compile-time rows are check 2. (b) Fixture placeholder: the hunk adds a line assigning a round literal (1.0f, 0, 4) with no comment to a field of a model-parameter or configuration struct that is then passed by pointer or reference to the function under test. (c) Opaque literal: the hunk adds an equality assertion whose expected side is 32 or more hex characters, or a table of four or more entries no test expression derives, with no provenance comment and no repository document containing it.
skill_entry.procedure: (a) Keep round trips, read-backs, kept partners and rows whose discarded bits are zero. For each other row name the storing accessor, search h/ and src/ for a reader, format or AGENTS.md line that depends on the exact bits (a policy or history comment is none), and compute the second policy (the generic converter, or the function a comment says 'would' differ) on the row's input. (b) Follow the struct to the first production call; in the hardware implementation, not the stub, record the field as read on the exercised path, read in an unreached branch, or never read. Evaluate the production producer on the fixture's own values: never read and unequal is a placeholder. Count repeats in every touched test file. (c) Read upward to the first blank line or def/TEST_CASE for a comment naming a generator, date, revision or copied-from file:line; grep documents for the literal; grep AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, if present, for a register mandate.
skill_entry.question: Name what depends on this exact value: for a conversion row, the production reader, format or repository rule that breaks if it changes; for a fixture literal, the exercised line that reads the field; for an opaque literal, the command, date and source revision that produced it, and the register row that lists it. If nothing does, say so next to the value or drop the row.
skill_entry.do_not_fire:
- pair-invariant rows when the test or its accessor cites the Note naming the dependent path; otherwise ask for the citation.
- regression rows for a failure seen on main or in the product; rows pinning a documented wire, file or hardware format.
- a fixture literal equal to the production producer evaluated on the fixture's own values (`params.gqa = 4` with `n_heads = n_kv_heads * 4` equals src/tron/gof.cpp:65 `n_heads / n_kv_heads`; the callee reads gqa no more than pre_attn_scalar).
- a fixture literal the exercised callee reads (a wrong stimulus is a correctness finding), or one already commented as a placeholder.
- a literal that exists at BASE on a re-spelled call (API migration); positional aggregate or constructor arguments.
- an opaque literal whose constant or docstring names an authority, generator or revision; a commit id quoted as a citation; a digest used as a lookup key for a golden artifact (`reference_logits`); digests in generated .json files.
- never recompute a value or dispute a tolerance.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (a) "This row makes '<input> stores as <output>' a tested contract. <AGENTS.md:line '<rule>' | no reader in h/ or src/ depends on <policy>; the only statement is the test comment '<quote>'>. Suggest dropping <rows> and keeping <the round trip and the partner-zero checks>." (b) a suggestion block on the first assignment: "<field> = <literal>; // not correct, but it's a don't-care for this usage below" then "and similarly elsewhere this is done" with the repeat lines; hits in other files of the same PR go on a second line of the same finding. (c) a question: "is this 'magic' <digest|table> captured or documented anywhere? Where did it come from? Are these supposed to be listed in <register doc> (referenced from AGENTS.md:<line>)?"; with no register, ask for a comment naming the command, date and revision.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Kind (a): normal, a declarative statement with the repository rule named and a 'Suggest dropping ... and keeping ...' ask; no severity word. Kind (b): no severity word; the whole comment is a ```suggestion block with the comment text plus the sentence 'and similarly elsewhere this is done'; the author replied 'fixed in commit 8a6db7243'. Kind (c): normal, a question in three parts ('captured/documented anywhere? Where did it come from? Are these supposed to be listed in ...'); the author replied 'Good catch: it was not registered.' None of the three blocks the PR; he approved PR 2176 (3969129694 at 8e19ea3e62), asim 244 (5240537644 at 63c5b8a12c) and PR 4557 (5431977719 at c5d44bd86f) after the fixes.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the row, the assignment, the assertion); full test files the diff touches (repeat count of a fixture block across files; the comment block above an assertion up to the first blank line); other files (the hardware implementation of the callee, not the stub; the production producer of the field; the generic converter); repository policy files at HEAD when they exist (AGENTS.md test-policy line, NaN rule, register mandate; CLAUDE.md) and the register document itself (docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md in asim). A test file at the review commit, fetched with gh api contents when the PR diff shows only the merged head. Not callers, PR body, commits, CI or runtime. Boundary: a round literal in a t/ fixture belongs here (kind b); a bare literal on an added h/ or src/ line belongs to the magic-literal check.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 1: value-pinning rows need a consumer; fixture placeholders a don't-care comment; opaque literals a provenance

BASE for this check (and the common setup): a merged PR whose base branch is not main gives an empty diff under `merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` (it returns HEAD) and a 30-file diff under `origin/main` (PR 2176: 25 step-9 hits instead of 4). Use the PR's recorded base: `BASE_SHA=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/<repo>/pulls/N --jq .base.sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $BASE_SHA)` (PR 2176 at HEAD 635de61895: base sha 363edb2910, BASE 1794cdf67d, 19 files).

Steps 1-8 unchanged (conversion rows, kind (a)). Steps 9-14 are new.

9. Fixture placeholders, kind (b). Print HEAD lines directly: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- 't/*' 'tests/*' | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3); next} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); n=a[2]; next} /^\+/{ if ($0 ~ /^\+[ \t]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\.|->)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*[ \t]*=[ \t]*(1\.0f?|0\.0f?|[0-9]+)[ \t]*;[ \t]*$/) print f":"n": "$0; n++; next}'`. It lists added assignments of a round literal to a struct field with no trailing comment. Record the struct variable (`params`) and the field (`pre_attn_scalar`). A literal that exists at BASE on the same statement (an API re-spelling such as `push(0, ...)` to `push(process_device_id{0}, ...)`) and a positional aggregate or constructor argument are not hits.
10. Callee: `grep -n -E '&<var>\b|<var>\)' full/<file>` from the assignment downward to the first production call that takes the struct (PR 2176: `xfer_blocking(..., &params, ...)`). `git -C WT grep -n '<callee>' HEAD -- h src` returns every implementation, including a stub (src/pos/fake.cpp, empty bodies). Open the implementation the test binary links on hardware (the file under src/pos/ that is not fake.cpp): `git -C WT show HEAD:<callee file> | grep -n -E '<param>->|\.<field>'`. Record per field: READ on the exercised path (stop, not a placeholder), READ in an unreached branch, or NEVER READ. Record the stub separately as "stub, reads nothing"; a field the hardware implementation reads is READ.
11. Real producer: `git -C WT grep -n '<field>' HEAD -- h src`; pick by reading the line that computes the production value. Evaluate it with the fixture's own values. For gqa: src/tron/gof.cpp:65 `gof_params.gqa = n_heads / n_kv_heads` with the fixture's `n_heads = n_kv_heads * 4` gives 4, equal to the literal: not a placeholder. For pre_attn_scalar: h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:396 `1.0f / sqrtf(head_size)` (635de61895; :395 at 429249ead6) with head_size 128 gives 0.088, so 1.0f is a placeholder. A literal is a placeholder when the exercised callee NEVER READs it and it differs from the producer evaluated on the fixture's shape.
12. Repeats: `grep -n '<field> = <literal>' full/*` over every test file the diff touches, plus every step-9 hit in another file. The finding is one suggestion block on the first line plus "and similarly elsewhere this is done" listing the repeats in the commented file; hits in other files of the same PR go on a second line of the same finding, never as separate findings. A pre-existing line that step 9 did not list (not added by the PR) is mentioned at most as pre-existing.
13. Opaque literals, kind (c): assertions `grep -n -E '^\+.*(\b(REQUIRE|CHECK)[A-Z_]*\(|\bassert\b)[^/]*\b[0-9a-f]{32,}\b' pr.diff` (word-bounded, so CHECKPOINT does not match); frozen tables `grep -n -E '^\+.*(\b(REQUIRE|CHECK)[A-Z_]*\(|\bassert\b).*\[(\s*0x[0-9a-f]+\s*,){3,}' pr.diff`; a literal bound to a name first `grep -n -E '^\+\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\s*=\s*"[0-9a-f]{32,}"' pr.diff` (digits allowed in the name; on asim 244 this finds RTL_REVISION, EXP_TABLE_SHA256 and FROZEN_D128_CHECKPOINT_DIGEST), then follow the name into an assertion. Use grep -E, not awk, for `{32,}` (mawk ignores the interval). Map to file:line at HEAD. `gh pr diff N` shows only the merged head: to run at the commit next to a comment, fetch each touched test file with `gh api 'repos/<org>/<repo>/contents/<path>?ref=<commit>' --jq .content | base64 -d > full/<path>` and grep it; a hit is a finding only if the line is also an added line of the PR diff. A table is a hit only on the expected side of an equality assertion; GENERATE rows, stimulus fractions and tolerance arguments are never an expected side.
14. Provenance: read upward from the assertion to the first blank line or the enclosing `def`/TEST_CASE line, whichever comes first (`sed -n '<start>,<line>p' full/<file>`), and keep only a comment that names a generator, a date, a source revision, or the production file:line the table is copied from (`g_dequant` in t/t_clearhbm.cpp at tron-2475 cites h/tron/hardware/quantization.hpp:99 and is not a finding). A comment stating what the value must stay equal to is not a provenance. `git -C WT grep -n '<first 12 hex characters>' HEAD -- docs doc '*.md' '*.json'`. Register mandate: `git -C WT show HEAD:AGENTS.md | grep -n -i -E 'regist|anchored|evidence|provenance|frozen'`, same for CLAUDE.md; if the file does not exist at HEAD (`git show` fails, as at 635de61895), record "no register mandated" and continue. Register present and literal absent -> the finding asks for the origin and the register row, citing the AGENTS.md line that names the register. Register absent -> the finding asks for a comment with the generating command, the date and the revision. A literal whose definition carries an authority or revision line (EXP_TABLE_SHA256 under "Authority: executable RTL <sha>") is not a finding; a digest that selects a golden artifact for a tolerance comparison (`reference_logits`, t/testutil.hpp:33, `check_golden_logits`) is a lookup key, not an expected value.

On PR 4557 (kind a): tables at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3573-3577 and :3609-3612 (96a6220ab6); B rows :3574 (0x3f80ffff), :3577 (tie 0xbf818000), :3610 (65504 fp16); C row :3575 (0x7f800001 -> +inf, AGENTS.md:73-75 "Treat NaN as corruption"); test-policy line AGENTS.md:35-38 ("identifiable consumer"); second policy h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:57-69 and :89-105 (fp32s_to_bf16s keeps the NaN); kept A rows :3561-3563, :3601, :3647; P rows :3544, :3640. Outcome at c5d44bd86f: rows :3574, :3575, :3577, :3610 gone, sections renamed "float rows are stored as bf16 and keep the pair rule" (:3547) and "fp16 rows are stored as bf16 and keep the pair rule" (:3582).

On PR 2176 (kind b, HEAD 635de61895, BASE 1794cdf67d): step 9 prints t/t_hwattention.cpp:93 `params.gqa = 4;`, :94 and :571 `params.pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f;`, t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp:217 `attn_params.pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f;`. Step 10: the fixture feeds `k_block.xfer_blocking(tok_ix, dev->idx, k_hbm, layer, &params, false)` at :104-105; `git grep xfer_blocking` returns src/pos/hwattention.cpp:107 and :117 (calls xfer) and src/pos/fake.cpp:129 and :135 (empty); hwattention.cpp xfer at :18-19 and :48-49 reads only `params->kv_head_size` and `params->n_kv_heads`: pre_attn_scalar and gqa NEVER READ on this path (the FPGA launch path reads pre_attn_scalar at src/pos/worker.cpp:931, logs it at :936; h/tron/models/model.hpp:794 forwards it; none of these runs in the test). Step 11: pre_attn_scalar producer h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:396 `1.0f / sqrtf(head_size)` (inside the else of `if constexpr (softcapping)` at :391; the gemma branch at :392-393 uses query_pre_attn_scalar) and :399 `hw_attn_cfg.pre_attn_scalar = rsqrt_pre_attn_scalar`; 1.0f equals neither: placeholder. gqa producer src/tron/gof.cpp:65 `n_heads / n_kv_heads` = 4 on the fixture: not fired. Step 12: repeats :94, :571, :1029, :1174 in t_hwattention.cpp; other-file hit t_hwattention_replay.cpp:217; pre-existing t/t_gof_dma.cpp:68 (not added, not a hit). Outcome at 8a6db7243 (Brian Hamon, 2026-03-18, "Address PR #2176 review feedback", ancestor of 429249ead6): :94, :571, :1029, :1174 read `params.pre_attn_scalar = 1.0f;  // not correct, but a don't-care here`; at 429249ead6 the lines are :95, :575, :1033, :1178; t_hwattention_replay.cpp:217 stayed uncommented and Wade approved (3969129694 at 8e19ea3e62), so the other-file line is a nit the author may decline. Step 14 at 635de61895: AGENTS.md absent, "no register mandated".

On PR asim 244 (kind c): `gh pr diff 244 --repo positron-ai/asim` is the merged head (5619 lines); the corrected assertion regex gives 0 hits there, the named-literal regex gives RTL_REVISION, EXP_TABLE_SHA256 and FROZEN_D128_CHECKPOINT_DIGEST. The file at 3e71b6c4d4 via gh api contents (154 lines): step 13 hits tests/test_qwen35_native_reference.py:40 `assert digest.hexdigest() == "14afab7ff0d8..."` (the comment was posted at cef64ea5bd, review 5215895996, where the assertion sat at :39). Step 14: the block above runs without a blank line from :24; the comment at :31-32 ("Frozen from this independent v1 reference before the tie-order correction; all 282 untied D128 checkpoint arrays must remain byte-identical under v3") names no generator, date or revision (a five-line window would see no comment at all); 0 of 314 .md files at 3e71b6c4d4 contain the literal; AGENTS.md:147-149 mandates "The registry `docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md` lists the registered anchored files"; the register lacks the row at 3e71b6c4d4. Not fired: src/asim/validation/native_precision.py:33-34 `RTL_REVISION` / `EXP_TABLE_SHA256` under the docstring line :7 "Authority: executable RTL f5d4da20ad..."; tests/test_native_precision_reference.py:41-42 cites commit 8e4cfabac9 as the source of the tie cases. Outcome at 927d501a86: constant `FROZEN_D128_CHECKPOINT_DIGEST` at :12 with a provenance comment :7-11 (digest definition, "frozen 2026-09-11", "Registry: qwen35-native-tiny-reference-digest"), the assertion message :45-49 names the registry row, and docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md:191 carries the row; approved 5240537644 at 63c5b8a12c.
